children: Obstacles for farmers harvesting crops is providing support for crop basis prices, says Brian Hoops of Midwest Market Solutions. "Harvest activity remains limited due to wet conditions and rainfall across the Midwest, which support basis levels," says Hoops. Crop basis, the amount over or under futures prices buyers of grains are paying in different regions, is elevated versus this time last year for both corn and soybeans, according to data from StoneX. The weather forecast from the NOAA says that a rain system is expected to sweep through the Corn Belt over the next two weeks, potentially keeping farmers from being able to hit their fields to harvest mature crops. Corn settled down 0.5%, soybeans down 0.1%, wheat down 0.4%.(kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
